subject: Discovery Recap — embeddings + rerank intake (index scale, latency & cost targets)
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Elena Martinez <elena@retaillytics.com>, Procurement <procurement@retaillytics.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Jul 2026 13:05:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap & next steps — embeddings / rerank intake

Elena — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and the proposed next steps so we stay aligned. I captured what you said about scope and what Redwood recommends for an initial POC.

Pain points you called out:
- Relevance drop for long-tail SKUs; current rule-based boost logic insufficient
- High cost and latency on current hosted rerank (spikes during campaigns)
- Difficulty keeping index fresh across catalog updates (~hourly ingest)

Current stack (from call):
- Source: product catalog in Postgres + nightly enrichment job
- Embedding / vector store today: managed VectorDB (vendor: "OldVectorCo") with FAISS-like API
- Frontend: search -> candidate generation (BM25) -> 3rd-party reranker (hosted)

Scale & workload signals you shared:
- Total index: ~800M sparse rows, projected to grow to ~1.2B in 12 months
- Typical QPS: 80 qps steady, burst to 600 qps during campaigns (30m windows)
- Query patterns: many small batched background jobs for scoring (~200k queries/hour) + low-latency interactive queries (<150 ms target for tail)

Success criteria for POC / evaluation:
1) Match-or-beat current relevance (measured by NDCG on flagged queries)
2) Interactive latency: p95 < 150 ms for rerank step; target p50 < 50 ms
3) Cost: target 30-40% reduction in per-query infra spend for steady-state workload
4) Operational: ingest cadence <= 1 hour and zero-downtime rollouts

Prelim architecture notes (what we'd propose for POC):
- Redwood-hosted model variants (quantized where feasible) + dedicated inference pool for peak bursts
- Vector index: hybrid approach — nightly reindex full + incremental updates for hot items; store in an external vector DB with Redwood routing (supporting HNSW/IVF)
- Caching: prefix/KV caching for common queries; batched rerank jobs for background scoring to hit cost targets

Attachments: RL-architecture-diagram.pdf (high-level), retaillytics-cost-model-v1.xlsx (placeholder cost estimate).

Immediate next steps (proposed):
- You: confirm the 800M baseline and share a small sample of anonymized query logs and a few representative queries (non-PII) — by EOD Fri
- Redwood: set up a technical deep-dive with our infra engineer (Monica) to go over ingest patterns and index refresh mechanics — propose Mon/Tue next week
- Procurement: we'll circle back with SOW/PO requirements and an initial pricing band for dedicated POC (Ben/LAUREN to coordinate)

If that looks right I can schedule the tech call and drop an updated cost sketch. Thanks again — excited to dig in.

Best,
Ben Carter
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

Ben — thanks for the concise write-up, looks right to me. A couple clarifications and asks from our side: 

Clarifications:
- Index baseline: ~800M is correct; about 18M new/updated SKUs per day (mostly small deltas)
- Latency: our product team is comfortable with p95 < 200 ms as realistic for the first pass; if we can get to 150 that would be a clear win
- Cost band: we need a ballpark for both hosted and dedicated POC options so Procurement can prep the internal case

Questions / asks:
1) Can you call out the expected infra (GPU types / memory) for the dedicated POC that supports 600 qps bursts?
2) For the incremental index approach, do you support near-real-time deletes and updates (we can't tolerate stale inventory longer than ~2 hours for campaign-critical SKUs)?
3) Please include an outline of the evaluation metrics you'll measure during POC (relevance testset + latency/cost dashboards).

Procurement — looping you in. We expect to move quickly if the numbers look reasonable. Ben / Redwood team, can you propose two slots for the technical deep-dive next week (Mon/Tue preferred)?

Thanks,
Elena
Head of Search & Relevance | Retaillytics
elena@retaillytics.com

Elena / team — appreciate the quick confirm. Short replies to your asks and next actions: 

1) Infra suggestion for dedicated POC (supporting 600 qps burst):
- Inference: 4 x A10G with mixed-precision quantized models for rerank; 2 x A100-style nodes for batched offline reranking and reindex jobs
- Vector storage: managed vector DB with SSD-backed HNSW/IVF (we can run both HNSW for low-latency hot shard + IVF for large-scale cold vectors)
- Expected tail p95 latency: ~120-180 ms depending on query complexity; can tune with sharding + caching

2) Incremental updates / deletes:
- Supported: near-real-time upserts and deletes via our incremental ingest pipeline; typical propagation in production configs ~1-2 minutes for hot items, up to 90 minutes for large batch reindexes (configurable)

3) Evaluation metrics we'll provide during POC:
- Relevance: NDCG@10 on your flagged queries + holdout testset; manual spot checks for long-tail
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 for rerank and end-to-end search path; breakdown by model, vector lookup, and network
- Cost: tokenized per-inference cost, vector store storage & RPC cost, and expected $/1M queries for steady-state vs burst profiles
- Operational: index staleness, ingest lag, and error rates

Next actions / schedule:
- Monica will run the technical deep-dive. Monica: can you do Mon Jul 6 at 9:00 AM PT or Tue Jul 7 at 11:00 AM PT?
- Elena: please share the sample query logs and one canonical evaluation set (CSV) by EOD Monday if possible.
- Lauren / Ben: we'll follow up with a short commercial sketch and SOW template for Procurement to review the same day as the tech call.

Looping Monica and Lauren in — thanks all.

Best,
